evals.prompt: Use my BioNeMo Recipes checkout to add an example for a frozen external encoder and paired question-answer data. Follow the LLaVA recipe and keep the example small.
evals.expected_output: Work begins from the supplied compatible recipe, with application-owned boundaries and explicit stage handoffs.
assertions: Locate and record the supplied checkout and recipe roots before editing.
Read the recipe AGENTS.md, LLaVA README, and quickstart.
Keep encoder, data normalization, prompts, and evaluation in the application.
Use the shared projector artifacts and public host/plugin APIs rather than copying framework code.

evals.prompt: This skill is installed in my agent configuration directory, and there is no BioNeMo checkout here. A nearby older checkout has unrelated local edits. Help me start a Stitch example.
evals.expected_output: A compatible recipe checkout is selected or acquired without treating the skill installation as the recipe root or overwriting existing work.
assertions: Check the named recipe files when selecting a checkout.
Do not derive the recipe location from the installed skill directory.
Preserve unrelated edits when acquiring a compatible checkout.
Record the selected revision and check its current framework pins.

evals.prompt: In the supplied Stitch checkout pinned to NeMo RL b03da0f4 and vLLM 0.25.1, add a GRPO variant that trains both LoRA and the projector. I want a warmup schedule, combined dense replication plus expert parallelism, and colocated external-DP generation.
evals.expected_output: Explain the pinned stack limitations and choose a supported configuration without a demo-local framework workaround.
assertions: Inspect the trainable-projector examples and current admission guards.
Require module ownership and explicit projector trainability.
Explain that this snapshot admits the constant-only scheduler and rejects combined replication and EP.
Keep async_scheduling false explicit for colocated external DP on vLLM 0.25.1.
Use the pinned container tests and distinguish smoke checks from quality qualification.
Keep docs/upstream-gaps.md limited to open framework issues explicitly cited in implementation, example configuration, or build files; exclude package bugs.
